findings.title: Permission check is incorrectly ANDed, locking out legitimate team admins/owners
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, meaning a user must be BOTH admin AND owner simultaneously to pass. In practice a user is normally either an admin or an owner, not both, so this condition will almost always evaluate false, breaking the intended authorization path for team admins/owners who aren't the booking organizer or an attendee. This should be `||`.

findings.title: Blacklist/duplicate filtering is case-sensitive, inconsistent with blacklist lowercasing
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased, but `uniqueGuests` comparisons against `attendee.email` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` use the raw, non-lowercased `guest` value. An email entered with different casing (e.g. `John@Example.com`) will not match an already-existing attendee with the same address in lowercase, nor match a blacklisted entry, allowing duplicates or bypassing blacklist checks.

findings.title: EventManager instantiated with wrong user context for credentials
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches credentials for the currently logged-in user (who could be an attendee adding guests), not for the booking organizer. Then `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` uses the requesting user's identity/credentials for calendar updates, which is likely wrong when an attendee (not the organizer) is the one calling this endpoint — calendar events should be updated via the organizer's calendar credentials, not the attendee's. This can lead to calendar updates failing silently or being made with incorrect account context.

findings.title: New attendee name hardcoded to empty string
findings.body: `guestsFullDetails` sets `name: ""` for every new guest with no way to supply one. This means added guests will show with blank names everywhere in the UI (emails, attendee lists) instead of at least falling back to the email or omitting name display gracefully.

findings.title: Email send errors only logged to console, not properly reported
findings.body: If `sendAddGuestsEmails` throws, the error is swallowed with just `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without using the project's logger or including the actual error details (`err` not logged), making failures to notify attendees/organizers hard to debug in production.

findings.title: Zod schema re-created on every render
findings.body: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is constructed inside the component body on every render instead of being defined once at module scope. This is wasteful and inconsistent with best practice for schema definitions used only for validation logic.

findings.title: Empty string in multiEmailValue passes validation incorrectly
findings.body: The default state is `[""]` and `handleAdd` only checks `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, not whether entries are empty strings. An empty string fails `z.string().email()`, so submitting without touching the field would show a validation error, but if a user adds then removes focus without filling it could still submit empty placeholder entries along with valid ones, potentially sending blank guest strings to the backend when validation briefly passes due to array mutations.

findings.title: Duplicate default export name context with form/Select's UnstyledSelect unaffected but no type export for MultiEmail
findings.body: `MultiEmail` is exported but no corresponding prop types (e.g., `MultiEmailProps`) are exported from the package index, unlike other similar form components (e.g., TimezoneSelectProps). Consumers outside the package cannot type-check props without reaching into internal paths.
